blocks.text: Veterinary epidemiologist Robert Sanson later documented the development of the spatial work after those first weeks. Varroa_sim was programmed in ArcView using Avenue and treated 9,229 registered North Island apiaries with valid map-grid coordinates as the population at risk. The stochastic model represented local spread, movement within a beekeeper's operation and the seasonal concentration of hives for pollination, while eradication assumptions could be changed through menus in the map interface. The work also exposed a quieter data problem. Apiary map-sheet references were subsequently converted automatically to full New Zealand Map Grid coordinates and validation was added to stop impossible locations entering the database. GIS was therefore doing two jobs: modelling where infestation might move and forcing the underlying location records to become more dependable.
